cards.title: A push or a pull
cards.idea: A force is simply a push or a pull acting on an object.

interaction.prompt: Tap the actions that are a push or a pull: kicking a ball, thinking about a ball, opening a drawer, dreaming

cards.reveal: Kicking a ball and opening a drawer are forces. Thinking and dreaming are not, because nothing is pushed or pulled.

cards.title: Force needs a direction
cards.idea: A force always acts in some direction, so we draw it as an arrow pointing that way.

interaction.prompt: Tap the arrow that shows the force when you pull a drawer toward yourself

cards.reveal: The correct arrow points toward you, the direction of the pull. A force has both a size and a direction.

cards.title: Force can change speed
cards.idea: A force can make a still object start moving, speed up a moving object, or slow it down.

interaction.prompt: Drag the football to show what happens after you kick a resting ball

cards.reveal: The resting ball starts moving in the direction of your kick. The force changed its speed from zero to moving.

cards.title: Force can change direction
cards.idea: A force can change the direction in which an object is moving, without necessarily stopping it.

interaction.prompt: A moving carrom coin is struck from the side. Tap what changes.

cards.reveal: Its direction changes. A sideways force can turn a moving object onto a new path.

cards.title: Force can change shape
cards.idea: A force can also change the shape of an object, like squeezing dough or stretching a rubber band.

interaction.prompt: Tap the objects whose shape a force can change: dough, a stretched rubber band, a steel rod pressed lightly

cards.reveal: Dough and a stretched rubber band change shape easily. A steel rod barely changes under a light press, but a force still acts on it.
